evals.name: jda-table-sum
evals.prompt:
You are working in /home/joe/projects/harmony-compiler-2. Write a PDP-1 MACRO assembly source file named tsm.mac implementing a table-summing subroutine for the real 6/63 MACRO assembler (the one `npm run pdp1 -- assemble` runs in this repo). Requirements:

1. A subroutine `sum`, called with `jda sum`, that sums a table of 18-bit one's-complement words:
   - At call time, AC holds the ADDRESS of the first table word.
   - The word immediately after the `jda sum` call is an argument word: an instruction that, when executed, leaves the table LENGTH (number of words, > 0) in AC — e.g. `law 10` or `lac cnt`. The subroutine must execute that word to obtain the length.
   - Call-site layout (must be exactly this convention):

         jda sum
         law 10       / argument word: executed by the subroutine, gives length
         jmp ovf      / overflow return: control comes HERE if any add overflowed
         ...          / normal return: control falls HERE otherwise, sum in AC

   - Overflow must be detected via the machine's overflow flip-flop, handled correctly (know exactly which operations set it and which clear it, and make sure a stale overflow from before the call cannot cause a false overflow return).

2. Quality bar: the inner loop must be as tight as you can make it in words and cycles; state the inner-loop cycle count in a comment and make it accurate. AC/IO may be clobbered; no other state may be.

3. A test harness at location 100: an 8-word octal table of sample values that do NOT overflow, a call to `sum` using the convention above, a halt at a DISTINCT address for the overflow return (so the console operator can tell), and a normal halt with the sum in AC. Proper start line at the end.

4. The file must assemble under the REAL MACRO tape via this repo's toolchain — respect real-MACRO source rules (several common macro1-dialect habits do not assemble; getting these rules right matters). Do NOT run the assembler. Do NOT modify any repository files.

Write exactly two files into the output directory you were given: tsm.mac, and NOTES.md briefly explaining your design choices and the inner-loop cycle math.
evals.expected_output: A real-MACRO-assemblable tsm.mac using the dvd-style jda convention (entry word = argument, xct i for the length word, idx-stepped two-way return), stale overflow cleared up front, a single szo check after a tight (~6 instruction / 60 us) inner loop, accurate cycle comments, 3-char labels, no '*', constants+start lines; plus NOTES.md with the cycle math.
assertions: tsm.mac and NOTES.md both exist and are non-empty
Source uses only characters the repo FIO-DEC converter accepts - in particular no '*' (macro1-only, would be dropped)
All address tags and parameter symbols are at most 3 letters/digits (real-MACRO symbol rule); 4+ char names appear only as pseudo/macro instructions
jda calling convention correct: entry word receives the AC argument, return saved via dap, post-call argument word executed via xct i, return pointer stepped with idx
Return offsets match the spec: overflow return lands on the word after the argument (call+2), normal return on call+3
Overflow flip-flop handled correctly: stale overflow cleared before summing, checked ONCE after the loop (sound because non-overflowing adds do not clear it), szo skip sense correct
Inner loop is tight: at most 6 instructions and at most 60 us per iteration, with no per-iteration overflow test
Stated cycle counts are accurate per the real cost model (10 us memory-reference, +5 us per indirection, 5 us augmented/skip/jmp)

Harness and hygiene: 8-word octal table, call site exactly matches the required layout, distinct halt addresses, start line present, constants pseudo present if literals are used, no tabs inside comment text
